requirement:
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
rationale:
The workflow obligations are all carried out by `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`, and one test verifies them. I found no gaps.

Obligations, each mapped to the skill's Workflow steps and Rules:
- **Move with own edits, kept separate from any change to the moved code or text.** Step 1 says "Make the move with your own edits… Change nothing else in this step". The Rules add "Move first, run the command, commit, then edit".
- **Run `habeas refactor --dry-run` with a mapping for every moved file, node and definition name.** Step 3 asks for one `--map <old>=<new>` for every moved file or directory, node and definition name. It gives the file or directory, `<file>#<selector>` and definition-name forms, which match `requirements.refactor.mappings`. The step is a dry run, in line with `requirements.refactor.dry_run`.
- **Review the report, including records left unchanged and the rationale spans it lists.** Step 4 covers "Would rewrite", "Would change" with the rationale code spans that still mention an old path, and "Would leave … unchanged". This matches `requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`.
- **Run without `--dry-run`.** Step 5.
- **Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale.** Step 6.
- **Commit the move and evidence update before changing behavior.** Step 7.
- **Then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill.** Step 8.

Test: `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_moves_first_then_updates_evidence_with_habeas_refactor]` carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It uses `assert_in_order` to check that the key phrases of each step appear in the order the requirement lists them. It also uses `assert_phrases` for the "never edit evidence by hand", "a rename is not a move" and "editing moved code in the same step leaves records stale" rules. `bundled_skill` collapses whitespace, so phrases that wrap across lines in `SKILL.md` still match.

No unspecified observable behavior is added. The extra advice in the skill, such as `git add` and `habeas info`, is guidance and not code behavior.

text: :::{req} refactor_skill.workflow
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
:::{req} dry_run
With `--dry-run`, `habeas refactor` MUST report every change it would make,
in the same form as {cite}`requirements.refactor.command`, and MUST write
nothing.
:::{req} mappings
Each `--map` MUST have one of these forms:
- a file or directory path, which maps that file, or every file under that
directory, to the same relative path under the new side;
- `<file>#<selector>`, which maps one outline node, and its outline
descendants, to the node at the new file and selector;
- a definition name, which maps that full name, and every full name beginning
with it followed by `.`, to the same suffix under the new name.
A mapping whose old side names a recorded definition, or a prefix of one
followed by `.`, MUST be a definition-name mapping.
:::{req} rationale.untouched
`habeas refactor` MUST NOT change rationale text other than the spans
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.names`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.paths`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.addresses` cover. For each changed
record, it MUST list the other code spans in the rationale that contain an old
side of a path or node mapping, so the user can review them.
